newsitem.title: USA: Samsung starts Alpha chip test production.
newsitem.headline: Samsung starts Alpha chip test production.

text.p: Samsung Electronics Co Ltd said Monday it had begun test production of its version of Digital Equipment Corp's Alpha microprocessor, the first product to result from an alliance of the two companies.
In a statement Samsung said limited samples of its Alpha 21164 chips are now available, and general sampling will begin in January 1997 at speeds ranging from 366 megahertz to 500 megahertz.
Samsung said it will begin mass production of the Alpha 21164 family in the second quarter of 1997 at its advanced eight-inch fabrication plant located in Kihueng, South Korea.

As the world's sixth largest semiconductor maker, Samsung said it will take advantage of its technology and high volume manufacturing expertise to drive down the price of Alpha chip technology in 1997, thereby expanding its potential markets.

Samsung said its chip is fully compatible with Digital's Alpha 21164 family. It plans to demonstrate the chip in an Alpha-based workstation runnning Microsoft Corp's Windows NT at the Comdex trade show next week in Las Vegas.
The Digital-Samsung deal allows Samsung to become an alternate, second source manufacturer of current and future versions of Digital's high performance Alpha microprocessors.
In addition, the deal granted Samsung a license to market, sell and distribute Alpha microprocessors worldwide.
